That record's issue text: C# runs the clear and the event as TWO loops (CombatManager.cs:492-499 then :500-507), so AfterBlockCleared fires for every participant including 'one whose clear a ShouldClearBlock listener prevented', and it names 'Sturdy Clamp is a ported Rare relic in ALL_RELICS (relics/sturdy_clamp.py:23-25; SturdyClamp.cs:22-29)' as one of the two ported preventers alongside BarricadePower, with the observed numbers '[sturdy_clamp, horn_cleat] also 0' block at turn 2 where C# gives 14, and '[sturdy_clamp, captains_wheel] with 0' at turn 3 where C# gives 18. guards.what: G2 (LIVE): the cap has no PREVENTER test and runs from the wrong hook at the wrong point in the turn
guards.issue: This is audits/seam/turn_structure.json gap G2, which that record raised specifically about this relic, so per binding rule 3 the verdict is cited and matched. Its mechanism: Creature.ClearBlock (Creature.cs:718-728) passes the vetoing listener OUT of Hook.ShouldClearBlock and fires `Hook.AfterPreventingBlockClear(preventer, creature)` on the else-arm; SturdyClamp.cs:31-46 caps the retained block at 10 there and opens with `if (this != preventer || creature != Owner.Creature) return;`. sts2_rl/hooks.py defines no such hook and hooks.should_clear_block returns a bare bool, so sturdy_clamp.py:27-30 caps from on_player_turn_start instead -- with no preventer test and AFTER the energy reset (player.py:163-169), where C# caps inside AfterTurnStart, before the AfterBlockCleared loop and before SetupPlayerTurn. The consequence the seam proves: Hook.ShouldClearBlock returns the FIRST vetoing listener (Hook.cs:2193-2204) and CombatState.IterateHookListeners walks a player's POWERS before that player's RELICS (CombatState.cs:412-435), so with Barricade AND Sturdy Clamp held the preventer is BarricadePower, Sturdy Clamp's cap never runs, and C# keeps the FULL block. RE-EXECUTED for this record (py tools/audit/relic_probes_b15.py b15-clamp, calling player.start_turn() in isolation so the enemy's attack cannot eat the block and confound the read): 30 block with [sturdy_clamp] -> 10 (correct), 30 block with Barricade + [sturdy_clamp] -> 10 where C# gives 30, 4 block -> 4 (correct), and no relic -> 0 (correct). Both sides ported and obtainable: Barricade is an Ironclad Rare Power card (cards/barricade_card.py, powers.py:140) and Sturdy Clamp is Rare in the grab bag. Pinned in the seam as test_sturdy_clamp_does_not_cap_when_it_is_not_the_preventer (verified by grep).

guards.what: G3 (DORMANT): C# skips the whole ClearBlock call on the player's TURN 1, so neither ShouldClearBlock nor AfterPreventingBlockClear is consulted; the sim runs both
guards.issue: MECHANISM, and this is a third divergence the seam's G1/G2 do not cover: Creature.AfterTurnStart opens with `if (side == CombatSide.Player && player.PlayerCombatState?.TurnNumber == 1) return;` (Creature.cs:681-691), so ClearBlock() -- and therefore Hook.ShouldClearBlock and Hook.AfterPreventingBlockClear -- never run at all on the player's first turn. PlayerCombatState.start_turn has no such early return: it calls should_clear_block unconditionally (player.py:157) and sturdy_clamp.py:29-30 then caps the block on turn 1. EXECUTED (b15-clamp): the sim records `t1 should_clear_block`. Consequence: a player entering combat with more than 10 block keeps all of it in C# and is capped to 10 by the sim. REACHABILITY (DORMANT, executed census): an AST scan of every sim on_combat_start body finds exactly ONE that touches block -- powers.py:1054, PlatingPower, whose combat-start grant is `if self.owner.side == 'enemy'` -- so no ported effect can give the PLAYER block before turn 1's start_turn, and the player enters every combat at 0 block (Player.AfterCombatEnd does LoseBlockInternal(Block), Player.cs:833-838). What makes it live: porting a player-side Plating, an event or relic that grants combat-entry block, or any BeforeCombatStart block grant above 10. This is the same turn-1 exemption audits/seam/turn_structure.json G1 alludes to ('a player on turn 1 whose AfterTurnStart returned early') but does not verdict as its own divergence; recorded here because it is Sturdy Clamp's cap, not the event, that it changes. Rule 7: leans on player.py, powers.py and Creature.cs, none hashed here.

guards.what: N1: `player.block = 10` (sturdy_clamp.py:30) vs `CreatureCmd.LoseBlock(creature, block - 10)` (SturdyClamp.cs:42), and the `block != 0` / `block > 10` structure
guards.rationale: Arithmetically identical -- losing (block - 10) from block leaves exactly 10 -- and the direct assignment cannot skip a side effect here, verified in both directions. C# side: CreatureCmd.LoseBlock (CreatureCmd.cs:666-678) fires Hook.AfterBlockBroken only when `block > 0 && creature.Block <= 0`, and this call is guarded by `block > 10` so the result is always exactly 10 > 0 -- AfterBlockBroken can never fire from the cap. Sim side EXECUTED (b15-clamp): a sentinel with an after_block_broken listener records NOTHING when the cap fires on 30 block. C#'s outer `if (block != 0)` exists only to skip the Flash on a zero-block turn, and the inner `block > 10` matches the port's `if player.block > self.MAX_RETAINED`. The constants agree three ways: `_maxRetainedBlock = 10` (SturdyClamp.cs:14), BlockVar(10m, ValueProp.Unpowered) (SturdyClamp.cs:18) and MAX_RETAINED = 10 (sturdy_clamp.py:21), with no AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension anywhere in the file.

guards.what: N2: `creature != base.Owner.Creature` on both overrides (SturdyClamp.cs:24, 33) vs `creature is not self.player` / the un-guarded on_player_turn_start
guards.rationale: should_clear_block IS dispatched for enemies in the sim (combat.py's enemy turn-start arm), so sturdy_clamp.py:25's identity test is load-bearing and correct -- it lets every enemy clear normally, exactly as SturdyClamp.cs:24-28 returns true for a non-owner. The cap's own owner test is structurally satisfied because on_player_turn_start is only ever dispatched for the player (player.py:169). Note that C# compares CREATURE IDENTITY here rather than SIDE, and so does the port, so there is no side-vs-identity divergence of the kind relic/unsettling_lamp G3 records.
